title: Sepsis, severe sepsis, septic shock, urosepsis and bacteremia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the sepsis, severe sepsis or septic shock only (not the local infection or the organ dysfunction). If none applies, choose 'no code'.
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026
Reason for Admission: Sepsis and skin infection

Vitals: BP 128/74, HR 82, SpO2 96% on RA, Temp 98.6 F

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Positive for fever, malaise
Integumentary: Positive for erythema, localized pain
Respiratory: Negative for shortness of breath
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain

HPI: Patient is an 89-year-old female who presented to the emergency department with a painful, erythematous area on her left lower extremity. She reported a history of minor skin abrasions and noted increasing warmth and drainage over the last 48 hours. She denies any systemic symptoms prior to the onset of fever.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted for treatment of sepsis originating from a skin infection. Cultures were positive for methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA). She was started on intravenous cefazolin. She responded well to antibiotic therapy, remaining hemodynamically stable throughout her stay. She was transitioned to oral medications before discharge.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Sepsis
MSSA skin infection

Discharge Medications:
Cefazolin 500mg every 8 hours (complete course)
Acetaminophen 650mg every 6 hours as needed for pain

Follow-up:
Follow up with primary care physician in 7 days for wound evaluation.

Electronically signed, 
P. O'Brien, MD
05/15/2026
explanations: Sepsis due to methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus: A41.01 (HCC 2).
